questions.text: Statements: All interns are students. All students are library members. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.B: Some library members are not interns.

questions.explanation: Interns are inside students, and students are inside library members, so every intern is a library member. The reverse ('all library members are …') doesn't follow: there may be library members who aren't students.

questions.text: Statements: No pilots are smokers. All captains are pilots. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?
questions.explanation: Every captain is a pilot and no pilot is a smoker, so no captain is a smoker. Whether some pilots aren't captains isn't stated: all pilots could be captains.

questions.text: Statements: All cyclists are helmet owners. Some teachers are cyclists. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.D: Some teachers are not helmet owners.

questions.explanation: The teachers who are cyclists are also helmet owners, so some teachers are helmet owners. We know nothing about the other teachers, so 'all teachers' and 'some teachers are not' don't follow.

questions.text: Statements: Some doctors are runners. Some runners are vegetarians. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.A: It is not true that all runners are doctors.

questions.explanation: None follows. The runners who are doctors and the runners who are vegetarians may be different people or the same people, so 'some doctors are vegetarians' and 'no doctors are vegetarians' can each be false. Every runner could also be a doctor, so 'it is not true that all runners are doctors' doesn't follow either.

questions.text: Statements: No volunteers are paid staff. Some organisers are volunteers. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.A: Some organisers are not paid staff.
options.C: Some paid staff are not organisers.

questions.explanation: The organisers who are volunteers can't be paid staff, so some organisers are not paid staff. The other organisers may or may not be paid staff, so 'no organisers are paid staff' doesn't follow.

questions.text: Statements: All sprinters are athletes. No chess players are athletes. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?
questions.explanation: Every sprinter is an athlete and no chess player is an athlete, so no sprinter is a chess player. 'Some athletes are not sprinters' doesn't follow: all athletes could be sprinters.

questions.text: Statements: All managers are graduates. Some team leaders are not graduates. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.A: Some team leaders are not managers.
options.C: Some managers are not team leaders.

questions.explanation: The team leaders who aren't graduates can't be managers (every manager is a graduate), so some team leaders are not managers. It could still be that every manager is a team leader.

questions.text: Statements: All engineers are problem solvers. No artists are engineers. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.B: Some artists are not problem solvers.

questions.explanation: None follows. Artists are outside the engineers, but that says nothing about whether they are problem solvers: 'no artists are problem solvers' and 'some artists are problem solvers' can each be false.

questions.text: Statements: Some volunteers are retirees. All volunteers are first-aiders. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?
questions.explanation: The retirees who are volunteers are first-aiders (every volunteer is), so some retirees are first-aiders. Nothing is said about the other retirees.

questions.text: Statements: No smokers are marathon runners. Some club members are marathon runners. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.B: Some smokers are not club members.
options.D: Some club members are not smokers.

questions.explanation: The club members who are marathon runners can't be smokers, so some club members are not smokers. Other club members could be smokers, so 'no club members are smokers' doesn't follow.

questions.text: Statements: All contracts are signed documents. No signed documents are drafts. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.C: Some signed documents are not contracts.

questions.explanation: Every contract is signed and no signed document is a draft, so no draft is a contract. 'Some signed documents are not contracts' doesn't follow: every signed document could be a contract.

questions.text: Statements: No freelancers are pension members. No pension members are part-timers. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?
questions.explanation: None follows. Two 'no' statements only say that freelancers and part-timers are both outside pension members; they may overlap completely, partly or not at all.

questions.text: Statements: All nurses are shift workers. All nurses are first-aiders. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.B: Some first-aiders are not shift workers.

questions.explanation: The nurses are both shift workers and first-aiders, and there is at least one nurse, so some shift workers are first-aiders. 'All shift workers are first-aiders' goes too far: there may be shift workers who aren't nurses.

questions.text: Statements: All apprentices are mentees. All mentees are workshop attendees. No workshop attendees are remote workers. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.C: Some workshop attendees are not apprentices.

questions.explanation: Apprentices are inside mentees, mentees are inside workshop attendees, and no workshop attendee is a remote worker, so no apprentice is a remote worker. The reverse inclusions don't follow.

questions.text: Statements: Some suppliers are exporters. All exporters are registered traders. No registered traders are tax-exempt businesses. Assuming the statements are true, which conclusion must follow?

options.A: Some tax-exempt businesses are not suppliers.
options.C: Some suppliers are not tax-exempt businesses.

questions.explanation: The suppliers who are exporters are registered traders, so they can't be tax-exempt: some suppliers are not tax-exempt businesses. Other suppliers might be tax-exempt, so 'no suppliers are tax-exempt businesses' doesn't follow.
